+# Tutorial 08 — OpenClaw x402 Payments Plugin
+
+| Information         | Details                                                                 |
+|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| Tutorial type       | Task-based                                                              |
+| Agent type          | Single, payment-enabled                                                 |
+| Agentic Framework   | [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)                                         |
+| LLM model           | Any (Claude, Nova, GPT, Gemini — configured via OpenClaw)               |
+| Components          | OpenClaw Gateway, `@aws/openclaw-x402-payments` plugin, AgentCore Payments, x402 |
+| Example complexity  | Beginner                                                                |
+
+> **Zero code required.** This tutorial installs an [official AWS plugin from ClawHub](https://clawhub.ai/packages/@aws/openclaw-x402-payments) and walks through the entire payment setup and usage via natural conversation with your AI agent.
+
+---
+
+## What You Build
+
+An AI assistant that **transparently pays for x402-paywalled content** through natural language. When the agent encounters a paywall, it automatically:
+
+1. Detects the HTTP 402 response
+2. Extracts the x402 payment challenge
+3. Signs a payment via AWS AgentCore Payments (Coinbase CDP wallet)
+4. Replays the request with the signed proof
+5. Returns the unlocked content
+
+No Python scripts. No manual API calls. Just install, configure, and ask.
+
+---
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
+User (Discord / WhatsApp / Telegram / CLI / Web)
+  │
+  └── OpenClaw Gateway
+       │
+       └── @aws/openclaw-x402-payments plugin
+            │
+            ├── 1. Agent fetches URL → HTTP 402 + x402 challenge
+            ├── 2. Plugin calls ProcessPayment (AgentCore SDK)
+            │       └── AgentCore → Coinbase CDP wallet → EVM signature
+            ├── 3. Waits for validAfter (EVM clock-skew handling)
+            ├── 4. Replays request with X-PAYMENT header
+            └── 5. Returns 200 + paid content to user
+```
+
+---
+
+## Why This Approach?
+
+| Pattern | Code required | Setup time | Best for |
+|---------|--------------|------------|----------|
+| Strands agent (Tutorial 01) | Python script | ~30 min | Developers building custom agents |
+| LangGraph agent (Tutorial 01) | Python script | ~30 min | LangGraph-based workflows |
+| Browser agent (Tutorial 05) | Python + Playwright | ~45 min | Browser-rendered paywalls |
+| **OpenClaw plugin (this tutorial)** | **None** | **~5 min** | **Existing OpenClaw users, non-developers, fastest path to payments** |
+
+The `@aws/openclaw-x402-payments` plugin is an **official AWS plugin** published on [ClawHub](https://clawhub.ai/packages/@aws/openclaw-x402-payments) — the OpenClaw plugin marketplace. It's verified, source-linked, and maintained alongside these samples.
+
+---
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- **OpenClaw** installed (version `2026.3.24` or newer — plugin system required)
+  - Install: `npm install -g openclaw` — see [docs.openclaw.ai](https://docs.openclaw.ai)
+- **AWS account** with AgentCore Payments access (preview)
+- **AWS credentials** configured (`aws sts get-caller-identity` to verify)
+- **Coinbase CDP API key** — get one at [portal.cdp.coinbase.com](https://portal.cdp.coinbase.com)
+
+> **Testnet only.** All payments use Base Sepolia (Ethereum) with free USDC from [faucet.circle.com](https://faucet.circle.com/). Testnet USDC has no real-world value.
+
+---
+
+## Step 1 — Install the Plugin
+
+```bash
+openclaw plugins install clawhub:@aws/openclaw-x402-payments
+```
+
+This downloads the plugin from ClawHub, verifies its integrity, and installs it to `~/.openclaw/extensions/x402-payments/`.
+
+Verify installation:
+
+```bash
+openclaw plugins list
+```
+
+You should see `x402-payments` in the output.
+
+---
+
+## Step 2 — Set Up Payment Infrastructure
+
+The plugin includes a `setup_x402_payments` tool that creates your entire payment stack in one conversation. Start a chat with your OpenClaw agent and say:
+
+> **You:** "Set up x402 payments for me"
+
+The agent will guide you through:
+
+1. **Provide your CDP credentials:**
+   - CDP API Key ID (UUID from portal.cdp.coinbase.com)
+   - CDP API Key Secret (Ed25519 key)
+   - Wallet signing key (EC P-256 — generate with: `openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout | openssl ec -outform DER | base64`)
+   - Email address (for wallet linking)
+
+2. **Agent creates the infrastructure:**
+   - Payment Manager
+   - Credential Provider (with your CDP key)
+   - Payment Connector
+   - Wallet Instrument (your on-chain wallet)
+
+3. **Agent returns your wallet address and funding instructions.**
+
+> **Alternatively**, if you already completed [Tutorial 00](../00-setup-agentcore-payments/), you can skip the agent-guided setup and configure the plugin directly with your existing resources:
+>
+> ```bash
+> openclaw config patch '{
+>   "plugins": {
+>     "entries": {
+>       "x402-payments": {
+>         "enabled": true,
+>         "config": {
+>           "region": "us-east-1",
+>           "paymentManagerArn": "YOUR_PAYMENT_MANAGER_ARN",
+>           "paymentInstrumentId": "YOUR_INSTRUMENT_ID",
+>           "userId": "YOUR_USER_ID",
+>           "networkPreferences": ["eip155:84532"]
+>         }
+>       }
+>     }
+>   }
+> }'
+> ```
+
+---
+
+## Step 3 — Fund Your Wallet
+
+Go to [faucet.circle.com](https://faucet.circle.com/):
+
+1. Select **Base Sepolia**
+2. Paste the wallet address from Step 2
+3. Request testnet USDC
+
+Wait ~30 seconds for the transaction to confirm.
+
+---
+
+## Step 4 — Create a Payment Session
+
+Ask your agent:
+
+> **You:** "Create a payment session with a $5 budget"
+
+The agent calls `create_payment_session` which:

Strengthened the guidance in Step 4 with:
- "The agent MUST request explicit user approval before creating any session"
- "Review the budget amount and duration before approving every single time"

This makes it unmistakably clear that autonomous spending without consent is not acceptable.

commented_code:
+# Setup Reference
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+### AWS Account Setup
+
+1. **Enable AgentCore Payments** in your AWS account (available in us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-2)
+2. **Create an IAM role** with the following trust policy:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Version": "2012-10-17",
+  "Statement": [
+    {
+      "Effect": "Allow",
+      "Principal": {
+        "Service": "bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com"
+      },
+      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+3. **Attach permissions** to the role:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Version": "2012-10-17",
+  "Statement": [
+    {
+      "Effect": "Allow",
+      "Action": [
+        "bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentCredentialProvider",
+        "bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentManager",
+        "bedrock-agentcore:GetPaymentManager",
+        "bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentConnector",
+        "bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentInstrument",
+        "bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentSession",
+        "bedrock-agentcore:ProcessPayment",
+        "bedrock-agentcore:GetPaymentSession",
+        "bedrock-agentcore:GetPaymentInstrument"
+      ],
+      "Resource": "*"
+    },
+    {
+      "Effect": "Allow",
+      "Action": [
+        "secretsmanager:CreateSecret",
+        "secretsmanager:PutSecretValue"
+      ],
+      "Resource": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:agentcore-payments-*"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+### Coinbase CDP Setup

Fixed in d2b6927. Credentials now have explicit guidance to use `.env` files with a code example:

```bash
# .env (add to .gitignore!)
CDP_API_KEY_ID=your-key-id
CDP_API_KEY_SECRET=your-key-secret
CDP_WALLET_SECRET=your-wallet-secret
```

The plugin reads these from the environment at execution time. The LLM never sees the raw values — only the agent host process has access. This is also emphasized in the SKILL.md guidelines.

+# Weather Agent — Harness + Evaluations + Gateway + Observability
+
+![Weather Agent App](images/app_example.png)
+
+| Information         | Details                                                                    |
+|:--------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| Tutorial type       | Use Case                                                                   |
+| Agent type          | Weather assistant with multi-tool capabilities                             |
+| Agentic Framework   | None (direct boto3)                                                        |
+| LLM model           | Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5                                                 |
+| Tutorial components | Harness, Gateway (MCP), Guardrails (PII), Batch Evaluations, Observability |
+
+## Overview
+
